0.original: Alisaie would have you help her finish her patrol.

24.original: Scout the designated locations, and defeat any sin eaters that you find.

48.original: Here's what we'll do: I'll take the east side of the Inn, and you clear the west. That way you can have an undiluted experience with the resident terrors.

49.original: These marks on your map are where the usual trouble spots are.

50.original: You can assume that any beast with a white hide or carapace is a sin eater, but you'll know for sure soon enough when they come slavering after your aether. Remember: it's kill or be killed with these monsters.

51.original: Once you've slain whatever's prowling around out there, we can rendezvous back at the north entrance. Good hunting.

53.original: Ah, I thought there might be one or two lurking on the fringes. Nothing out of the ordinary for this area...

54.original: I expect you noticed it yourself, but individually, these lesser sin eaters are no more deadly than any natural predator you might encounter in the desert.

55.original: It's when they appear in numbers that they pose a threat. Much like the voidsent, they have an unfortunate tendency to flock to the strongest of their kind.

56.original: Thus when a powerful sin eater goes on the hunt, it might be attended by a veritable swarm of weaker kin. Imagine an army of such creatures descending on a village or hamlet...

57.original: That's the basic idea behind my patrols: to cull their ranks often enough that their numbers won't be overwhelming when the big ones come out to play. And you've certainly helped on that front.

58.original: Let's report our victories to Tesleen, shall we?

59.original: She hasn't been telling you stories, has she? Oh gods...

60.original: Alisaie tells me you helped out on her patrol. You have our thanks...and my apologies for leading you from one battle to another ever since the moment we met!

61.original: In any case, I'm glad to see the two of you found each other. You have no idea how badly Alisaie has missed your company! Everything is always, “If <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203> were here, <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> would─”

62.original: That's an exaggeration! And I don't sound like that, either! I was simply trying to view matters from another perspective, and I <hex:021A020203>respect<hex:021A020103> <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>'s methods!

63.original: Ahahaha! Honestly, after seeing <hex:02080DE905FF04686572FF0468696D03> in action, I can understand why.

64.original: The way <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> leaps into the fray without hesitation, it really is something to behold. I might be a little smitten myself!

66.original: Heh heh! I'm only teasing! Though I've no doubt <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> deserves all the admiration <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> gets. Just as you do.
